newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to get $80-100 mln loan from World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to get $80-100 mln loan from World Bank.

text.p: Croatia is close to completing a $80-100 million loan from the World Bank to help rehabilitate the country's banking system and restructure its large utilities, Deputy Prime Minister said on Thursday.

"A Croatian delegation and the World Bank have agreed in Washington on the so-called EFSAL (enterprise and financial sector adjustment loan)," Borislav Skegro, deputy PM for Commerce and Finance, told Croatian state television (HRT).
Skegro and other Croatian officials are now in the United States, holding investor presentations for the country's debut Eurobond, a $250 million five-year deal.
After the roadshows that also included Asia, the deal will be launched next week in London.
Skegro said the loan of between $80-100 million would be used to help overhaul Croatia's banking system and restructure and privatise large public sector firms.

The Croatian government late last year gave a green light for the overhaul of the largest ailing bank, Privredna Banka Zagreb at a cost of some $540 million. It has completed the recapitalisation of another three troubled banks -- Splitska, Rijecka and Slavonska.

It also decided to overhaul 16 troubled state-owned firms by shifting their debts to state banks and utilities, or covering them from the Privatisation Fund portfolio. It said it would need some $250 million to revive them.
The World Bank should approve the loan in March, Croatian state news agency HINA quoted Skegro as saying on Wednesday.
He did not mention the terms of the loan, but said they would be "very favourable."
Croatia has also reached a tentative agreement with the International Monetary Fund for a three-year 500 million loan, to be approved by the IMF board in mid-March and used for structural reforms.
